mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS trend is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC for the threshold condition is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate signal a dual threat of monetary tightening and economic weakness, which depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5%), the Federal Reserve typically initiates monetary easing, which boosts equity valuations and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE > 5% is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for residential construction, which supports economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises, or the Rank IC for HOUST trend is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 500,000 units, it signals a contraction in the residential sector that may foreshadow economic weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 500, or the Rank IC for the threshold condition is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a broad-based economic slowdown across manufacturing and construction, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a weak industrial production regime (INDPRO < 90), manufacturing output contraction signals an impending recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in economic deterioration.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 90, or the Rank IC for INDPRO < 90 is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
